applied.problem: "A real coil's wire resistance makes the lag a little under a quarter cycle and takes a few watts" is only true when the resistance is small beside X_L; a lab coil in lesson 6 or a large winding can lag well under 90° or take many watts.

The rule of thumb's "halve the current" when the frequency doubles holds only while the wire's resistance is small beside the reactance, but the qualifier covered only the lag; a coil with sizeable resistance does not halve its current.
"A real coil's resistance makes the lag a little less and takes a few watts" overstates how small the effect always is; it is small only when the resistance is small beside the reactance.
